problem: Smooth nonconvex nonconcave minimax optimization lacks theoretical guarantees for convergence rates even under favorable structural conditions like the two-sided Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality.
approach: Uses Lyapunov functions both for algorithm design and convergence certification; replaces an intractable idealized Lyapunov function with a computable gradient-based surrogate to derive TALDA, a single-loop algorithm that enforces Lyapunov descent by construction.
contribution: TALDA achieves linear convergence under the two-sided PL condition with explicit dependence on cross-smoothness, recovering existing rates while improving performance on weakly coupled min-max problems.

problem: LoRA-based continual learning methods suffer from incomplete knowledge transfer because they overlook task-shared directions and fail to identify truly task-specific directions when tasks are correlated.
approach: Proposes LoDA with task-driven decomposition that builds general and task-specific LoRA subspaces using energy-based objectives; learns robust up-projections via Gradient-Aligned Optimization and derives closed-form recalibration for knowledge sharing.
contribution: LoDA outperforms existing continual learning methods by decoupling knowledge sharing and isolation while maintaining robust performance.

problem: Spatial proteomics analysis remains fragmented with manual orchestration of heterogeneous tools, limiting research scalability and reproducibility for understanding tumor microenvironments.
approach: SP-Mind is an autonomous AI agent combining expert-curated biological skills with specialized computational tools to convert natural-language queries into end-to-end analytical workflows without task-specific fine-tuning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on SP-Bench (102 tasks across 18 categories) compared to existing open-source biomedical agent baselines.

problem: Compressing long chains of thought into compact tokens while preserving reasoning structure requires balancing global structure capture with fine-grained reasoning details.
approach: ImgCoT renders chain-of-thought as images and learns latent visual tokens instead of textual reconstruction, substituting linguistic bias for spatial inductive bias; loose variant augments visual tokens with selected key textual steps based on log-likelihood.
contribution: Enables compact encoding of reasoning with fewer tokens while retaining both global structure and details across multiple LLM architectures.

problem: Real-time diffusion-based compression requires lightweight models that generation-oriented pre-training fails to optimize for, and standard approaches are too slow for practical deployment.
approach: CoD-Lite uses compression-oriented pre-training paired with lightweight convolutions instead of transformers; distillation and adversarial learning enable one-step diffusion for real-time encoding/decoding at 1080p.
contribution: Achieves real-time 60 FPS encoding and 42 FPS decoding with 85% bitrate reduction compared to MS-ILLM.

problem: Spurious correlations causing models to learn wrong features remain difficult to address because group-balanced approaches require expensive bias annotations or pretrained models limited to interpretable biases.
approach: Reframes spurious correlations as class-conditional distribution mismatches and uses sample reweighting to maximize conditional entropy of labels given spurious factors, automatically highlighting minority groups.
contribution: Delivers competitive robustness to bias-supervised methods while eliminating need for bias annotations or predictions.

problem: Motion imitation evaluation metrics conflate policy limitations with intrinsic learning difficulty of target motions, preventing principled error diagnosis in physics-based humanoid control.
approach: Proposes Torque Variation Score (TVS), a physics-grounded metric measuring how torque magnitude must vary to correct pose perturbations, revealing which motions have flat reward landscapes and vanishing gradients.
contribution: TVS enables accurate error attribution: high error on low-TV motions indicates policy deficiency, while high error on high-TV motions reflects fundamental learning constraints; supports mocap quality control.

problem: Multimodal alignment fails under deployment shift because standard objectives entangle cross-modal dependence with marginal-sensitive geometry, lacking interpretable diagnostics.
approach: SSCA uses clipped soft-rank Gaussianization to suppress marginal effects, dependence-weighted sliced Wasserstein coupling for global alignment, and diagonal-stabilized block-spectral learning with auditable diagnostics for monitoring drift.
contribution: Improves robustness under perturbations and monotone distortions with reduced degradation compared to standard approaches; provides label-free, actionable diagnostic signals.

problem: Pruning at initialization methods lack rigorous theoretical characterization of global sparsity patterns that emerge at scale, limiting understanding of when and why they work.
approach: Connects discrete pruning heuristics to graph limit theory via graphons; proves masks converge to deterministic bipartite graphons, establishing topological taxonomy distinguishing homogeneous unstructured methods from heterogeneous data-driven methods.
contribution: Derives universal approximation theorem for sparse networks and connects limiting graphons to NTK-style generalization bounds with path-density interpretation.

problem: Generative models struggle with equality-constrained distributions because their support cannot match ambient space while satisfying manifold constraints, causing sampling instability.
approach: Perturbs data distribution in constraint-aware manner to increase support dimension while preserving manifold geometry; applies to both diffusion models and normalizing flows.
contribution: Enables stable sampling and data distribution recovery for equality-constrained generative models across representative scientific tasks.

problem: Source-free domain adaptation for regression lacks effective methods because continuous labels pose unique challenges for representation adaptation and pseudo-label refinement.
approach: Leverages discretized density-informed supervisory signals with instance-dependent weighting and auxiliary distribution learning to refine pseudo-labels and promote compact feature representations.
contribution: Demonstrates robust SFDA for regression under distribution shift with theoretical guarantees on perturbation resilience.

problem: Representing microbial dynamics in soil organic matter models requires connecting genomic data to biokinetic parameters, but the complex relationship between genomes and microbial processes remains unknown.
approach: Hybrid framework uses neural network to predict biokinetic parameters from metagenome-inferred functional traits while integrating ecological theory constraints ensuring realistic behavior even for unobserved state variables.
contribution: Improves generalization on synthetic and real genomic data; effectively learns dynamics of unmeasurable model components even with small datasets.

problem: Pretraining and post-training of reasoning models follow contradictory data-quality principles—large diverse pretraining versus smaller high-quality post-training—with unclear theoretical justification.
approach: Theoretically analyzes transformers on in-context weight prediction for linear regression; reveals balanced pretraining induces latent capabilities, SFT benefits from challenging examples, and RL favors large-scale non-difficult data.
contribution: Identifies key findings about dataset quality requirements at different training stages, validated on large nonlinear architectures.

problem: Simulating deformable objects under rich robot interactions requires jointly modeling environmental effects and robot-controlled dynamics without predefined physics.
approach: SoMA couples deformable dynamics, environmental forces, and robot joint actions in unified latent neural space using learned 3D Gaussian Splats for end-to-end real-to-sim simulation.
contribution: Improves resimulation accuracy and generalization on real robot manipulation by 20%, enabling stable long-horizon tasks like cloth folding.

problem: Adversarial distillation with robust teachers often fails because teacher confidence on unlearnable samples causes students to memorize spurious noise, leading to robust overfitting.
approach: Analyzes feature learning dynamics of two-layer networks to show teacher-student misalignment on Robustly Unlearnable Set drives robust overfitting; proposes using teacher uncertainty as robustness indicator.
contribution: Demonstrates robust overfitting is driven by teacher-student interaction on unlearnable samples; provides principled guideline via teacher predictive entropy.

problem: Zeroth-order optimization appears to work well for fine-tuning massive LLMs despite classical theory predicting dimension-dependent slowdown, leaving a theoretical gap.
approach: Derives one-step learning dynamics of ZO-SGD showing empirical Neural Tangent Kernel emerges with elements corresponding to inner products on random low-dimensional subspaces; invokes Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma.
contribution: Shows approximation error depends on model output size rather than parameter dimension, explaining ZO scalability to LLMs.

problem: Accelerated Noisy Power Method for PCA with inexact products requires overly restrictive perturbation bounds in prior work, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Provides improved analysis showing accelerated convergence under much milder perturbation conditions; proves analysis is worst-case optimal and derives accelerated decentralized PCA algorithm.
contribution: First decentralized PCA algorithm with provably accelerated convergence and similar communication costs to non-accelerated methods.

problem: Computing globally optimal policies in multi-agent systems with graph-structured local dynamics is intractable due to exponential state-action space scaling.
approach: Studies conditions for approximating optimal policies with local policies depending on m-hop neighborhood states; controls influence propagation using Dobrushin-type stability matrix.
contribution: Shows globally optimal policies can be approximated by local policies with sub-optimality gap decaying exponentially in neighborhood radius.

problem: Understanding dynamic point cloud sequences in multimodal LLMs is unexplored due to lack of large-scale datasets and difficulty modeling spatio-temporal motion.
approach: Constructs 4DPC²hat-200K dataset via topology-consistent 4D point construction and two-level captioning; proposes Mamba-enhanced temporal reasoning MLLM with failure-aware bootstrapping to iteratively strengthen reasoning.
contribution: First MLLM for dynamic point clouds with 44K sequences and 200K QA pairs; significantly improves action understanding and temporal reasoning.

problem: Risk prioritization in high-stakes decisions requires interpretability, but falling rule lists have restricted expressivity due to single-path structure.
approach: Introduces falling trees extending rule lists with tree-structured branching while preserving monotonic risk constraint; proposes GraviTree algorithm for learning Rashomon sets under depth and branching constraints.
contribution: Falling trees match or outperform FRL baselines with greater sparsity for high-risk cases; interpolates between rule lists and decision trees.

problem: Fairness research documents metric trade-offs but lacks quantitative frameworks to measure intrinsic compatibility without requiring causal graphs.
approach: Introduces game-theoretic framework decomposing metrics into interaction vectors; enables compatibility measurement via cosine similarity and mechanistic attribution to attribute coalitions.
contribution: Reveals fairness and utility are often structurally orthogonal rather than conflicting; debiasing improves fairness by compressing compatibility space.

problem: Unified multimodal models suffer from mutual impairment between understanding and generation branches due to incompatible inductive biases in supervision signals.
approach: DIVA framework transforms representation divergence into synergy by factorizing visual representation into shared and unique components based on complementary information flows; uses mutual information estimation.
contribution: Achieves improvements in visual understanding (+7.82%) and generation (+8.46%).

problem: Existing fake media research treats media authenticity and content veracity separately, overlooking how real-world deception jointly exploits both dimensions.
approach: FakeWorld 1.0 unifies authenticity and veracity assessment in omni-modal benchmark spanning text/audio/image/video with web-based presentation scenarios; introduces OmniChecker agent for joint detection.
contribution: Exposes fundamental capability limits in MLLMs for detecting high-fidelity mixed-source deception with explainable per-instance rationales.

problem: Transformer circuits lack stability assessment across different training runs, making it unclear whether reported circuits emerge universally or are instance-specific.
approach: Systematically studies attention-head stability across independently initialized refits in increasingly complex models; quantifies per-layer representational similarity and functional importance.
contribution: Establishes cross-instance robustness as prerequisite for scalable oversight; weight decay substantially improves stability; middle layers show strongest divergence.

problem: Training instability in deep learning stems from rare extreme gradient spikes causing oversized updates and optimizer corruption, requiring principled safeguards beyond gradient clipping.
approach: GradientStabilizer preserves gradient direction while replacing magnitude with statistically stabilized estimate from running gradient-norm statistics; proven uniformly bounded on spikes.
contribution: Improves training stability across LLM pre-training, quantization, ImageNet, RL, and forecasting; widens stable learning-rate regions with reduced divergence.

problem: Finetuning pretrained generative control policies requires expensive online experience collection; existing exploration relies on weak baselines.
approach: DF-ExpEnse leverages multimodal policy to create expressive candidate set; ensemble of critics identifies actions balancing quality with exploration interest; enables cross-agent communication in fleet settings.
contribution: Consistently improves finetuning sample-efficiency across manipulation and locomotion tasks compared to default and alternative baselines.

problem: Survey-based opinion elicitation relies on fixed questionnaires and static respondent sets, failing to adapt to partial responses across rounds.
approach: Proposes adaptive information elicitation framework jointly selecting queries and respondents based on information gain maximization; combines graph neural networks for imputation with information-theoretic criterion.
contribution: Achieves 12% relative improvement on CES at 10% respondent budget for population-level response prediction.

problem: Image-to-3D generation under occlusion lacks mechanisms to complete unseen regions while strictly preserving observed parts, requiring distinct control granularities.
approach: RelaxFlow decouples control granularity via Multi-Prior Consensus Module and Relaxation Mechanism; theoretically proves relaxation is equivalent to low-pass filtering on generative vector field.
contribution: Successfully steers unseen-region generation to match text intent while preserving visual fidelity; introduces ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D benchmarks.

problem: Standard conformal prediction breaks under domain shift in LLMs, leading to under-coverage and unreliable prediction sets despite finite-sample guarantees.
approach: DS-CP reweights calibration samples based on proximity to test prompt within conformal prediction framework, preserving validity while enhancing adaptivity.
contribution: Delivers more reliable coverage under substantial distribution shifts while maintaining efficiency; validated on MMLU benchmark.

problem: Machine learning Hamiltonian models predict orbital/density structures but lack evaluation as energy-force predictors, leaving unclear how well they perform for molecular dynamics.
approach: Proposes QHFlow2 with SO(2)-equivariant backbone and two-stage edge update; directly evaluates energy and forces from predicted Hamiltonians.
contribution: Achieves 40% lower Hamiltonian error with NequIP-level force accuracy and 20× lower energy MAE; demonstrates consistent scaling behavior.

problem: Language models generalize poorly beyond pretraining context lengths due to quadratic attention scaling, limiting long-horizon reasoning despite continued pretraining.
approach: L2A enables conditional token-wise long-range memory access by deciding when to invoke global attention; skips attention for ~80% of tokens via learned gating.
contribution: Extends Qwen context from 32K to 128K tokens with 3% performance loss; achieves 2× throughput and time-to-first-token improvements; enables 50% KV cache reduction.

problem: Graph structural entanglement from spurious correlations contaminates node embeddings, particularly affecting boundary nodes where structural noise blurs decision boundaries.
approach: BES selectively suppresses spurious structural noise at decision boundaries using adaptive contrastive learning GNN plug-in with minimal parameter perturbation.
contribution: Improves GCN performance by 3.3% average in node classification and achieves superior link prediction accuracy.

problem: Scientific data annotation bottleneck remains the last-mile verification and correction, which standard approaches ignore by discarding supervision in expert navigation strategies.
approach: Framework studies behavioral cloning on 9 synthetic annotation tasks simulating realistic human strategies; reveals hierarchical skill emergence and multi-task learning benefits.
contribution: Shows larger models are more data-efficient; multi-task pretraining enables efficient fine-tuning; models learn mistake representation generalizing across tasks.

problem: LoRA's low-rank assumption limits performance by failing to capture duplicated directions and update diversity in fine-tuning.
approach: Proposes LoKRA using Kruskal rank instead of matrix rank to characterize update diversity; LoKRA+ provides tighter theoretical lower bound.
contribution: Consistently outperforms LoRA across LLMs with state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks.

problem: LiDAR-based 3D detectors are vulnerable to adversarial attacks with incomplete disappearance difficult to achieve in physical settings.
approach: OBJVanish uses prompt-driven text-to-3D generation framework iteratively refining object/verb/pose to create LiDAR-invisible pedestrians under physical constraints.
contribution: Consistently evades six SOTA LiDAR detectors in simulation and real-world settings, exposing critical vulnerabilities in autonomous driving safety.

problem: Protein language models lack generalization across domain shifts encountered in real protein engineering campaigns, limiting practical utility.
approach: FLIP2 introduces seven new protein fitness datasets with splits measuring generalization relevant to engineering practice; evaluates suite of models.
contribution: Reveals simpler models often outperform fine-tuned protein language models, challenging utility of existing transfer learning techniques.

problem: Graph neural networks for dynamics modeling suffer from oversmoothing while unitary convolutions overconstraining smoothness despite physical systems requiring natural smoothing.
approach: Proposes relaxed unitary convolutions balancing smoothness preservation with natural smoothing required by PDEs; generalizes from graphs to meshes.
contribution: Outperforms transformers and equivariant networks on PDEs over complex meshes and weather forecasting.

problem: Egocentric video understanding requires maintaining spatial memory of object locations relative to user movement and answering long-horizon queries, which existing models struggle with.
approach: DirectMe incrementally constructs structured spatial memory from streaming egocentric observations, coupling perception with memory updates and spatial reasoning.
contribution: Significantly improves spatial reasoning of leading MLLMs on UCS-Bench with 170+ hours and 8.1K+ timestamped questions.

problem: Open-ended image-to-text generation in continual learning faces catastrophic forgetting when visual data distribution shifts over time.
approach: ECA employs Mixture of Query module for task-specific adaptation, Fisher Dynamic Expansion for structure growth, and embedding dictionary with replay to retain past knowledge.
contribution: Significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting; outperforms baselines on four new IL benchmarks reflecting real-world scenarios.

problem: Auto-bidding algorithms in digital advertising ignore the true marginal value of winning: the outcome difference between winning and losing accounting for organic alternatives.
approach: Models ad value as treatment effect and develops online learning algorithms for second-price auctions that exploit information revealed by payment rule.
contribution: Attains rate-optimal regret under several feedback models with improvement over first-price auction settings.
